questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go far away. I wanted to go to a place I had never been. Entire different culture and language. It was also important for me to go to lgbtqia+ friendly destination and Taiwan is both culturally different, speaks an entire different language but at the same time a very progressive country compared to other countries in East Asia.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Let's put Taiwan on people's radar? This country has so much to offer and I had the absolute best time here.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I had an amazing student volunteer from NTU. She did so much for me, I dont know what I would have done without her.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: My student volunteer. Like I wrote, she did so much work for. Others were not as lucky as me with their student volunteer, but I had an amazing volunteer. I also got a lot of emails from the school with information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer:
I wasnt so satisfied with assistance and orientation, especially since there wasnt any social stuff really which was really disappointing. We were introduced to student clubs in late March or something, way into the semester? That was way too late. 
My student volunteer provided all the assistance and orientation.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Facebook groups, make sure the place is airconditioned, make sure to videochat with the landlord.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its a big city - find some place near campus and make sure you know what campus youll attend since theres the main campus and then medical and public health is elsewhere in the city. Also, as a woman I would recommend finding an only-women flat, since I had a friend with really bad experience with mixed apartments (non-Taiwanese men)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My student volunteer

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Completely successful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get help from your student volunteer

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I guess a little bit repetitive of stuff i already knew. The level of academics were not super high, it was quite easy I guess.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Teaching was quite similar, although attendance was mandatory and counted in your grade which I absolutely HATED. You also had to mandatory assignments during the semester and presentation which I also absolutely hated.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: We were introduced extremely late to the clubs. Some says it was because it was the spring semester, supposedly the fall semester does it earlier.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds!!!! I didnt attend any, but there was supposed to be a lot!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Oh my god, there is so much but I didnt do it actually, so i dont know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Taiwan is SO BEAUTIFUL you can do anything here, anything you would like. You can see nature, hike, animals, cafes, historical sites, parks, go outside of inner taipei and see the surrounding areas. Public transportation is so good.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: So easy, cause the taiwanese is an amazing people. I have loved it here.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Actually, i didnt make a lot of student friends. A few, but not mainly i guess, so just be open and ready to chat!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Garbage system, food difference and level of english was very low... but it was not particularly challenging just different...

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Food, the indigenous people, buddhism, the beauty of the land, the language, the complex and rich history, their traditions, everything

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Prepare for not a lot of english-speaking with the taiwanese, you can eat ANYWEHERE and from ANY FOOD BOOTH and ALL THE FOOD IS DELICIOUS, and GET GOING TO TAIWAN and travel the island, it is beyond beautiful. Also, its cheap. And relies on cash.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use bumble bff is you have a hard time finding friends, its super nice and i met people there

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting my friends, seeing so much of the island, and getting the opportunity to study at a different university in the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Mandatory attendance in class

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: GET GOING TO TAIAN

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
